plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with showy colored bracts surrounding tiny yellow flower clusters called cyathia. In its native habitat it grows as a woody shrub up to 4 meters tall, and it is also grown widely as a potted holiday plant in the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: The colorful parts are modified leaves called bracts, not petals. The plant needs long uninterrupted nights of about 12 hours for several weeks to develop its color.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: An evergreen perennial with cup-shaped white flowers that fade to pink as they age. It blooms in cold weather and often pushes through snow, with bright yellow stamens at the center of each bloom.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; cultivated in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a true rose but a member of the buttercup family. Legend says it first bloomed from the tears of a girl with no gift for the Christ child.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading tree with a broad umbrella-shaped canopy and fern-like leaves. It produces large clusters of vivid flowers, each with one petal streaked with white and yellow, followed by long woody seed pods.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer and tropical dry season (November to January in places like Australia, southern Africa and Brazil)
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in tropical and subtropical regions
plants.funFact: Although it is celebrated for its spectacular flowers, it is endangered in its native Madagascar due to habitat loss.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: A dense evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and lightly fragrant flowers. It blooms earlier than the common camellia and is popular for hedges, espaliers and winter gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to mid-winter (October to January)
plants.location: Native to Japan and Taiwan; grown in mild climates in Asia, the southeastern US, Europe and Australia
plants.funFact: It is a close relative of the tea plant, and its seeds are pressed to produce camellia oil used in cooking and cosmetics in Japan and China.
